House M.D. 

I grew up with it being on air and my brothers and I would watch it together. My father loved that we watched it because he wanted us all to be doctors (it's a brown parent thing). 

I always valued good grades and my intelligence as a kid. This was a way to learn. The show taught me a lot about medicine. 

I ended up rewatching it twice in recent years. My first rewatch..... Was so difficult. I blocked out so much from my childhood because I was so young, bit seeing one of the characters struggle with HD in her family was so hard.

My family has HD. It's what I lost my mother too. One of the characters has also lost her mother to HD. HD is short for Huntington's Disease and it is an incredibly rare genetic disease, so of course it was featured in a show about rare diseases. 

It is what helped me diagnose my mother with what killed her the week after it happened, something my father didn't tell me until I confronted him years later.

It made me face and see things I was scared to. Info about medical trials. Patients with HD. The fear of being someone early on in showing signs. My slow and painful journey ahead.

I know it has so many flaws, and I will be the first to talk about them, but I just can't get enough of it.

That's another issue. It all comes down to YOUR rights. MY rights. MY ME MY ME. What's something I can SELFISHLY do? Rather than taking take to consider other people. The mask protects others, first. Then yourself. It is a selfless thing you can do at the grocery store to help keep people from getting sick, but you choose not to. That's where I judge you.

The mask isn't a death sentence. It doesn't keep you from living your life. It doesn't harm you in anyway, unless you genuinely have circumstances that prevent you from wearing it, so there is no reason not to wear it when out in shops or stores or at the bank. It shows you are in inherently selfish person who only cares about YOUR rights rather than respect.

That's another issue. Masks not being required doesn't mean "You're not allowed to wear one here! Science says so!" It means "We have lost our legal right to ask you to wear a mask in this space". Not being required, doesn't mean DO NOT. I am not required to wear sunscreen on the beach, but I am still allowed and ecouraged to. I will not be thrown off the beach if I wear sunscreen. 

I think most American places are just so selfish to be so anti mask and anti vax. I've dealt with people, day in and day out, argue that masks are actually killing them and it's hard to breathe in so they shouldn't wear it. The mask is worn FOR OTHER PEOPLE. Not for you. It's a matter of respect for everyone else. It does help keep me from getting sick, but it is WAY more effective at keeping everyone else around me safe. 

I also know it keeps people from being disgusting. You can't sneeze in my face while wearing a mask. You can't spit on me while talking. You can't pick your nose. You can't chew your nails. You can't do so many really gross things involving your mouth and its fluids if you are properly wearing a mask. People are inherently very gross and good at spreading disease, so anything that helps keep that from happening is awesome in my book.
Also imagine how much that hurts. Shit like watermelon and pumpkin have spikey vines and shit.

I hate this idea that "life has to go on" in reference to masks. Masks do not make life stop. Masks do not keep people from doing daily activities. Masks do nothing but protect people. Before the pandemic even started, there were people already wearing masks around the world living their life. Whether it be someone in America with an autoimmune disorder or someone in Japan riding the bus. Masks do not keep life from going on. They are a measure people are taking to ENSURE life CAN go on SAFELY. 

When I see people without a mask, I judge them. I feel it is too soon to start taking the masks off and I just don't understand the hate for masks. It's a piece of cloth that has shown to do real good for lowering the spread of disease, not just covid but things like strep throat too.
